previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, insulin-dependent diabetes, and prior MSSA leg infection was admitted for left lower extremity erythema and swelling concerning for recurrent cellulitis. He had elevated white count and lactate on admission but negative blood and imaging studies for abscess or DVT. IV vancomycin was started, later broadened to Zosyn. A skin biopsy showed findings indeterminate between early cellulitis and small vessel vasculitis, with a fungal culture positive for Pityrosporum yeast likely as a contaminant. The patient improved clinically with treatment, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with a PICC line for a two-week course of IV vancomycin and Zosyn, plus one week of oral Bactrim. Insulin regimen was adjusted for improved glycemic control, azathioprine was held, and follow-up was arranged with rheumatology and infectious disease.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the acute care service with 
spreading cellulitis left lower extremity and fever.  He had 
been discharged from the hospital 4 days ago on intravenous 
vancomycin and zosyn after resolution of the cellulitis.  After 
an ID outpatient visit, he was admitted for a concern for 
necrotizing fasciitis.  X-ray imaging of his left lower 
extremity showed subcutaneous gas.  Because of this finding, he 
was taken to the operating room for incision and debridment of 
the left lower extremity. His operative course was stable with a 
100cc blood loss.  He was extubated after the procedure and 
monitored in the recovery room.

His post-operative course has been stable. His vital signs and 
pedal pulses were closely monitored. His white blood cell count 
decreased to 9 from 13.  He was placed on intraveous pain 
medication. He continued on vancomycin, clindamycin, and zosyn 
as per infectious disease recommendation.  He remained NPO on 
intravenous fluids in anticipation of a return to the operating 
room for a dressing change.  Gram stain of the left leg showed 
no PMN's, wound culture showed no growth.

On POD #1, he returned to the operating room for left lower 
extremity washout and dressing change. A wound vac was placed on 
the left lower extremity at the close of the procedure.  His 
operative course was stable.  He was extubated after the 
procedure. On POD #4, he returned to the operating room after 
the patient reported increased leg pain and worsening of the 
cellulitis. The vac dressing was removed in the operating room 
and the patient underwent debridement of the necrotic tissue 
around the wound edges and muscle belly. The operative course 
was stable with a 100cc blood loss.  He was extubated after the 
procedure and his vital signs were monitored. The wound VAC 
remained off and moist dressings were applied twice daily. 

His regular diet was resumed after he returned to the surgical 
floor.  Vital signs were closely monitored. He resumed his 
insulin as per home dosing with blood sugar monitoring.  His 
white blood cell count has stabilized at 10.     

Infectious disease was consulted regarding the length of the 
antibiotic course.  It was recommended that he continue 
vancomycin and unasyn until ___, the clindamycin was 
discontinued on ___.  He has been tolerating a regular diet 
and has been afebrile.  The vac dressing was re-applied on ___. 
 He is preparing for discharge to a rehabilitation facility 
where he can further regain his strength and mobility. He has 
been scheduled to follow-up with Infectious disease in 2 weeks 
and with the acute care service.
